Last Friday (21st), the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case was delivered. In the early morning, police escorted a woman who had been queuing to attend the hearing into a police vehicle and took her away. In response to enquiries, the police said the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "seditious intention".

Shortly after 5am last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing a shirt with seditious intention", and took her away in a police vehicle. While officers were taking the woman away, several officers kept instructing reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled an orange cordon line towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, the cordon was taken down. A "court-watching volunteer" who was queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective Report enquired with the police about the reason the woman was taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (24th) that they had conducted a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, during which a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "seditious intention". She was detained for investigation.
